summary: US refueling tankers are being deployed to Israel and Jordan ahead of possible escalation with Iran, with five already en route and dozens to follow. Iranian forces attacked water desalination and power generation facilities in Kuwait, and US airstrikes continue against Iranian targets including bridges and surveillance towers. Jordan intercepted three Iranian missiles with no injuries or damage reported.
key_points: Five US Air Force refueling tankers are en route to Israel with dozens more to follow, likely escorting fighter jets to Israel or Jordan (Source: @N12chat/217889).
Iran attacked water desalination and electricity production facilities in Kuwait, with multiple power generation units damaged at the site (Source: @New_security8200/202696).
US forces destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari Port surveillance tower used by IRGC to track vessels in the Strait of Hormuz (Source: @shin_persian/8033).
Jordan intercepted three Iranian missiles fired at its territory with no casualties or damage reported (Source: @yediotnews25/132809).
A Thai-flagged ship was targeted in the Strait of Hormuz by IRGC naval forces after ignoring warnings and lacking passage permit (Source: @SharghDaily/172618).
Iranian airstrikes on Bahrain were intercepted according to a recent report (Source: @yediotnews25/132813).
US airstrikes on Iran for a fifth night reported seven killed, hitting a bridge between Bandar Abbas and Shiraz, Bushehr, and Iran Shahr airport (Source: @almogboker78/17730).
A wide US air bridge over Europe is moving many fighter aircraft to bases in Jordan and Israel (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/378369).

key_developments: Five US refueling tankers are en route to Israel with dozens more arriving Friday and Saturday at Israeli air force bases due to Ben Gurion congestion (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5067).
Iran attacked Kuwaiti water desalination and power generation facilities; Kuwait reported many electricity generation units damaged at the site (Source: @New_security8200/202696).
US forces destroyed the Chah Bahar Shahid Kalantari Port surveillance tower, an IRGC network node tracking Hormuz commercial vessels (Source: @shin_persian/8033).
Jordan intercepted three Iranian missiles with no casualties or damage, per an official announcement during ongoing US-Iran conflict (Source: @yediotnews25/132809).
A Thai-flagged vessel was targeted by IRGC navy in Hormuz after ignoring warnings and lacking passage authorization (Source: @SharghDaily/172618).
Fifth night US strikes in Iran reported seven dead; bridge Bandar Abbas-Shiraz, Bushehr, and Iran Shahr airport hit (Source: @almogboker78/17730).
Patriot system attempted intercept of attack on US base in Erbil; later a protest rocket launched from base at drone (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/378386).
sections.threat_assessment: The deployment of dozens of US refueling tankers to Israeli and Jordanian bases signals preparation for expanded strikes on Iran. Iranian retaliation has already extended to Kuwaiti desalination and power facilities and missile fire at Jordan and Bahrain, raising risk of regional infrastructure warfare. CENTCOM's denial of losses at Al-Tanf indicates active information operations around Syrian deployments. Continued US strikes on Hormuz-adjacent targets and Iranian threats to halt oil exports elevate the prospect of global energy disruption.
sections.regional_response: Jordan actively intercepted three Iranian missiles, demonstrating defensive posture against spillover. Kuwait acknowledged damage to critical utilities and did not report retaliation. Saudi Arabia faces Houthi-linked threats to its Red Sea bypass pipeline, per WSJ. The UAE has not asserted claims on the three islands since war began per a Persian channel. Yemenis in Sana'a demonstrated support for Iran per Press TV, indicating popular alignment against US-Saudi pressure.
sections.intelligence_notes: Iran's Supreme National Security Council directed media to avoid publishing damage to civilian infrastructure or service disruptions, using vague phrases (Source: @Faytuks_Network/5061). This complicates battlefield damage assessment. Reports from Ahvaz and Bandar Abbas describe repeated explosions and power cuts, partially corroborating strike claims. The Knesset dissolution and 32-month service extension show Israel preparing for prolonged mobilization. Verification of Iranian casualty figures from local channels remains unconfirmed by independent sources.
